Alani Nu Female Social Media Following
Record FY2024 revenue ~$1.36B (+3%); Q4 revenue and adjusted EBITDA each declined 4% - a return to 'more traditional results' after an 'uncharacteristic' Q3.
FY2024 net income fell 36% to ~$145M; Q4 a net loss of $18.9M, driven by one-time costs.
Q4 SG&A rose 73% to $185M on accrued legal expenses (case on appeal), Big Beverage acquisition costs, Center of Excellence build-out, legal settlement, and co-packer penalties/restructuring.
FY2024 gross margin expanded 220 bps to 50.2% on lower freight costs and raw-material savings.
Resilient operating metrics: 22% volume growth vs a 5% category, 37% points-of-distribution growth, ACV 98.7%, 30% of all 2024 category growth.
Dominant strategic news: a $1.8B definitive agreement to acquire female-focused functional wellness brand Alani Nu - cash + stock - expected to close Q2 2025.
Alani Nu deal creates a ~$2B pro-forma platform and ~16% combined energy category share; <3x 2024 revenue / ~12x fully synergized EBITDA; cash EPS accretive in year one.
$50M run-rate cost synergies expected over two years post-close (supply chain, sales force, back-office); pro-forma net leverage ~1x.
Alani Nu is incremental - a younger, aspirational female consumer (~92% female social following); management says cannibalization with Celsius is 'fairly low.'
Q1 2025 off to a 'slow start' in scanner data - attributed to promotion timing and cycling tough prior-year innovation comps (Essentials launch, strong Q1 2024 innovation), framed as timing-driven.
Category went negative in Q3 2024 for the first time in many years; steep new sugar-free competition gained trial.
The category is now >50% sugar-free; energy has 'gone mainstream' across all ages.

Contra revenue was a little elevated across 2024 vs 2023 and 2022; the largest-distributor incentive program will be fully in place by Q1-Q2 2025, with extra incentive in Q1-Q2 due to a phased-in approach.
Management deflected all questions on whether Alani Nu would migrate from the Anheuser-Busch network to Pepsi - 'running separate until closing.'
Tariff/aluminum risk could pull gross margin back ('high 40s with the tariffs'), but management defends ~50% as 'a solid number'; declined to detail Alani Nu's standalone margin until after close.
2025 spring resets expected to deliver ~15-20% Celsius distribution expansion and 'pretty sizable' Alani Nu convenience gains.
2025 innovation pipeline is back-half/summer-weighted (new flavors, CELSIUS HYDRATION, tentpole programs) - framed as the path to re-acceleration after a weak Q1.
Celsius begins selling in Subway starting March 2025 (18,000-location opportunity); also gained Home Depot distribution.
Alani Nu roughly where Celsius was two years ago in its growth cycle - meaningful ACV upside in foodservice and convenience.
Integration risk mitigants: the disciplined hiccup-free Pepsi integration precedent, active founder involvement, a two-year transition agreement, and founder equity alignment.
Celsius recently expanded internationally into the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand and France - 'just getting started in the first innings.'
Pepsi inventory rightsizing viewed as positive for long-term supply-chain health.
Management tone confident and forward-leaning, framing 2024 softness as timing-driven.
How the two brands would be positioned and whether there is age/demographic overlap to 'solve for.'

Alani Nu has a unique, incremental consumer base - a younger, aspirational, accessible female consumer centered on health/wellness/fitness, with a ~92% female social-media following. Cannibalization potential is 'fairly low,' with a much higher trade-in dynamic; Celsius gains two strong portfolios.
Whether the preference is to keep Alani Nu in the Anheuser-Busch network or consolidate it into Pepsi, and whether Pepsi would be involved financially or operationally.

Deflected the distribution question - the transaction was just announced and must clear customary closing procedures and regulatory approval, with an expected Q2 close. Praised the ABI network as a great partner; focus is on the consumer, customers and growing the businesses together.
Alani Nu incrementality vs core Celsius

Whether legacy Celsius would grow in line with the category with Alani Nu providing the lift, or return to above-trend growth; and how Alani Nu's powders/RTD shakes/snacks fit an energy-centric portfolio.

Acknowledged a 'slow start' in Q1 2025 from promotion timing and innovation comps but is bullish on the 2025 Celsius innovation strategy and 50/50 male/female positioning. The category is now >50% sugar-free; Alani Nu is roughly where Celsius was two years ago in its growth cycle with ACV upside in foodservice/convenience. Both brands form a better-for-you platform with adjacency expansion opportunities.
What to expect from spring shelf resets for core Celsius given challenged velocity trends, and visibility on shelf-space gains for Alani Nu.

Celsius expects ~15-20% distribution expansion within retail sets coming out of resets, with grocery and large-format leaning further into energy. Emphasized improved cold placements and disrupting the path to purchase. Alani Nu is expecting 'pretty sizable' distribution gains through reset season, especially in convenience.
Whether Pepsi has a right of first refusal for distributing other brands Celsius buys, who pays distributor buyouts if Alani Nu changes networks, the Q4 Pepsi inventory change, and Q1 expectations.

Reiterated focus on closing the transaction and servicing customers, with the companies running separately until close, declining the distribution-rights specifics. CFO quantified the Q4 Pepsi inventory change impact at between $8M and $10M.
Whether the near-term core slowdown expedited Celsius's push to get aggressive with M&A and buy scale, or whether Alani Nu had long been a contemplated target.

Celsius is 'extremely confident' in its portfolio and energy-category tailwinds; acknowledged the slow start and pointed to the 2025 innovation pipeline. The Alani Nu opportunity arose and is incremental; combining the two brands makes Celsius a ~16% energy-category share player (up from a solid #3) - a 'natural fit' leveraging built infrastructure and synergies.
Intra-quarter consumption trends for Celsius and Alani Nu, when velocity improvement should be visible, and how the new innovation pipeline is being received.

Reiterated confidence in the Celsius portfolio while acknowledging Q1 weakness from cycling high prior-year hurdles (Essentials launch, strong Q1 2024 innovation). Pointed to an innovation-packed back half into the summer beverage season, tentpole programs, and the 7-Eleven award; Alani Nu's incrementality and distribution gains will help. Framed the issue as timing; energy has 'gone mainstream.'
A diagnosis of the sequential share pressure across 2024 and how to address it, plus whether the Subway rollout is each franchisee's decision.

Attributed share pressure to category-wide challenges that emerged in Q3 2024 when the category went negative for the first time in many years, plus steep competition entering sugar-free and gaining trial. Path to recovery: Celsius's loyal long-term consumer, the 2025 innovation portfolio, targeted marketing, and broadening consumer-segment reach. (The Subway franchisee-decision portion was not directly addressed.)
How much promotional allowances impacted revenue and gross margin in the quarter, and whether the current gross margin level is sustainable given aluminum cost pressure.

Contra revenue was a little elevated across 2024 vs 2023 and 2022, with the distributor incentive plan fully in place by Q1-Q2 2025 and benefits from full program implementation expected to normalize the basis. On gross margin, tariffs are uncertain but Celsius is 'in good shape'; aluminum from Canada would not significantly impact results though it could pull margin back - conservatively 'high 40s with the tariffs,' but 50% is 'a solid number.' Declined to detail Alani Nu's margin profile until after close.
Key areas and visibility for the $50M synergy target and any upside, whether combined EBITDA margins could resemble Monster's US margins, and how Celsius limits integration risk.

Alani Nu is 18-24 months behind Celsius in life cycle, leaving leverage opportunity; the synergies are 'hard cost' - COGS, competitive purchasing power, a 500-strong sales force, global supply chain/procurement, back-office. Integration risk mitigants: the disciplined hiccup-free Pepsi distribution integration as precedent, active founder involvement, a two-year transition agreement, and founder equity alignment.

How Celsius will maintain Alani Nu's momentum (share gains roughly doubling YTD), what drove those gains, and why those consumers can be retained - implying some gains may have come at Celsius's expense.

Reiterated that the two portfolios combined add category strength and that the Alani Nu consumer is incremental. Energy-category consumers are loyal; Alani Nu has a true brand identity connecting emotionally with Gen Z and female Millennials, and the category has gone mainstream across all ages - supporting a massive growth opportunity.
Jeff Van Sinderen - B. Riley Securities
Alani Nu's current ACV and international penetration, and how Celsius plans to broaden its marketing reach in 2025 and how that changes with Alani Nu.

The international opportunity is 'massive'; Alani Nu has only a small amount of international distribution. Celsius itself recently expanded into the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand and France - 'just getting started in the first innings.' Cited the energy category at ~$90B in 2024 growing at a 10% CAGR to 2029. (Specific Alani Nu ACV and detailed marketing plans were not quantified.)
